subject: tourism
title: Model Question Paper 1
meta: Time: 3 hours · Maximum marks: 100 (with one optional module) · Modelled on the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: All questions are compulsory. Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Section A: MCQs carry 1 mark; objective questions carry 2 marks (two parts of 1 mark each).
Section B: very short answers 2 marks (30–50 words), short answers 3 marks (50–80 words), long answers 6 marks (80–120 words).
Section C: attempt either Optional Module I (Travel and Tour Operation Business) or Optional Module II (Hospitality Management) in all its questions.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Write any two positive economic impacts of tourism.
questions.answer: Tourism earns foreign exchange for the country and creates jobs for guides, hoteliers, taxi drivers and craftspeople. It also brings tax revenue to the government.

questions.q: Describe any two features of a General Reference Map.
questions.answer: It gives general information about spatial units such as the world, continents, countries, districts, cities, rivers, mountains and oceans. It is found in books and atlases, and an atlas is a collection of such maps.

or.q: Describe any two features of a Political Map.
or.answer: It shows international, state and coastal boundaries, state capitals, cities, ports, roads and railways. Different colours separate political units but no colour has a special meaning.

questions.q: Explain any two characteristics of the Bharat Darshan special tourist train.
questions.answer: It is an affordable package that covers important tourist places of the country. The fare includes accommodation in the coaches, tourist buses for sightseeing, hall accommodation at night halts and guides.

or.q: Explain two advantages of rail transportation for tourists.
or.answer: It is cheap and comfortable for long distances. A large number of people can travel together and the network reaches nearly all parts of the country.

questions.q: Describe any two characteristics of the musical instrument 'Veena'.
questions.answer: It is one of the oldest instruments, mentioned in the Vedic texts. The Saraswati Veena of South India is a plucked string instrument of the lute family used to accompany Carnatic music.

or.q: Describe any two characteristics of the musical instrument 'Shehnai'.
or.answer: It is an aerophonic tube-like instrument that widens towards the lower end. It is played at North Indian weddings and processions, and Ustad Bismillah Khan made it famous.

questions.q: Describe any two points of significance of Kedarnath as a popular destination for Hindu pilgrims.
questions.answer: It is the remotest of the Char Dham sites, on the Mandakini river near the Chorabari glacier in the Himalayas. Its temple is one of the holiest Hindu temples and is named after King Kedar.

or.q: Describe any two points of significance of Nalanda as an important centre of Buddhists.
or.answer: It was an ancient seat of Buddhist learning from the 4th to 12th century with 2,000 teachers and 10,000 students. Hiuen Tsang studied there and praised its education.

questions.q: Write a short note on Hazratbal as a holy place of Muslims.
questions.answer: Hazratbal stands on the bank of the Dal Lake in Srinagar and is the only bulbous-domed mosque in Kashmir. It is sacred because it keeps the sacred hair of the Prophet Muhammad.

or.q: Write a short note on a church as a holy place of Christians (Basilica of Bom Jesus).
or.answer: It is at Old Goa, built in 1605, a World Heritage monument. It holds the relics of St Francis Xavier and an exposition is held every ten years.

questions.q: Why did travel and tourism increase in recent decades in India? Explain any two reasons.
questions.answer: Rich countries' tourists had better finances and more leisure time for holidays and business trips. Better transport, accessibility, communication and accommodation also encouraged travel.

or.q: Explain spiritual tourism as an emerging dimension in India in two points.
or.answer: India is the confluence of Hinduism, Sikhism, Islam, Christianity, Buddhism and Jainism. Temples, mosques, monasteries and churches attract a huge number of domestic and international tourists.

questions.q: 'The trend of international tourist arrivals is almost continuously on the rise.' Support the statement with two relevant arguments.
questions.answer: World arrivals rose from 530 million in 1995 to 1,035 million in 2012 and 1,184 million in 2015. Arrivals grew every year since 2010 by about 4% or more, with only a small dip around 2003.

questions.q: Explain any two principles of effective writing.
questions.answer: Unity: sentences, paragraphs and the whole message should deal with one idea. Coherence: relation and clarity among sentences, so the message is clear.

questions.q: Explain any two importance of discount pricing.
questions.answer: It increases sales by offering a lower price in a season or on a quantity. It helps clear stock and attracts price-sensitive customers.

or.q: Explain any two principles of effective writing.
or.answer: Unity and coherence make the message one idea and clear. Accuracy and briefness make it correct and saves time.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Describe any three characteristics of road transportation.
questions.answer: (i) It gives basic accessibility, connecting places and people with flexibility and reliability. (ii) It is cheaper and can take the tourist up to the final destination. (iii) Highways, flyovers and different vehicles (cars, coaches, buses) connect rail, air and water transport.

questions.q: Analyse any three main features of the musical instrument associated with Lord Krishna (the flute).
questions.answer: (i) The flute (bansuri) is a wind instrument that makes sound from air flowing across an opening, and it is mentioned in the Vedic texts. (ii) It appears in the sculptures of Sanchi and Amaravati and the paintings of Ajanta and Ellora. (iii) Its volume can be increased by enlarging the resonator and tone holes, and it has also become a part of Western orchestra.

questions.q: Analyse the impacts of the British on Indian architecture in three points.
questions.answer: (i) Greek and Roman colonnaded buildings such as Parliament House and Connaught Place were built. (ii) Gothic and Indo-Saracenic buildings appeared, such as St Paul's Cathedral, Victoria Terminus and the Gateway of India, along with Lutyens's Rashtrapati Bhavan combining jaali and canopies. (iii) New cities, ports, railway terminals, hill stations, Civil Lines and cantonments were planned.

questions.q: Explain any three Jain heritage sites located in Rajasthan.
questions.answer: (i) Dilwara temples at Mount Abu, built in white marble with fine carving. (ii) Ranakpur temple (15th century) with 1,444 carved pillars and four marble statues of Rishabha. (iii) Jaisalmer, with intricately carved yellow-stone temples and a famous library of Jain manuscripts.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the significance of geography for tourism in six points.
questions.answer: (i) It helps in locating a place with latitude and longitude. (ii) It helps calculate the time-lag between source and destination. (iii) It helps set the time of a clock in a global context and adjust for the date line. (iv) Maps and charts show facts about places, transport and distances. (v) It explains the environment, climate and relief of the destination so that seasons can be chosen. (vi) It helps tourists understand and read different maps, such as political, road, railway and tourist maps.

questions.q: How is a road map important for tourists? Explain in six points.
questions.answer: (i) It shows the roads of an area and their condition in different seasons. (ii) It shows national, state and district highways and village roads in different ways. (iii) It shows petrol pumps, lodging and boarding facilities and places of public assistance. (iv) The distance matrix tells the distance between places, helping decide the journey and plan time. (v) It helps domestic tourists who travel by road choose routes. (vi) It helps reach destinations that rail and air do not directly serve.

sections.title: Optional Module I (Travel and Tour Operation Business): Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain any three functions of a travel agency.
questions.answer: (i) It quotes fares and rates and makes reservations for air, rail and hotel. (ii) It arranges tickets, accommodation, travel insurance, foreign currency and documents. (iii) It accepts payments and acts as a single contact for the tourist.

questions.q: Examine any three types of package tours.
questions.answer: (i) Escorted tour: a trained escort or guide accompanies the group and helps at every stage. (ii) Independent tour: tourists choose the components, so it is flexible but costlier. (iii) Incentive tour: a firm pays for its employees as a reward, e.g. a trip to Singapore.

questions.q: Why is it important for hotels to meet a guest's expectations? List the guest expectations on arrival.
questions.answer: (i) Meeting expectations earns luxury status, guest satisfaction and repeat business. (ii) On arrival guests expect a warm welcome, well-groomed and communicative staff and quick check-in. (iii) They also expect clean rooms, efficient luggage handling by the bell desk and recognition by name.

questions.q: Describe any three functions of the Sanitation department.
questions.answer: (i) It keeps the entire hotel clean to protect health. (ii) It ensures treatment and proper disposal of waste. (iii) It maintains gardens and the cleanliness of rooms with the housekeeping staff.
